granularity_detail: 0.25 degree grid (~28km). Partial because only an indirect proxy (Universal Thermal Climate Index, UTCI) exists - no dedicated heat-stress index.
0.25 degree grid (~28km), via dedicated Hot Days, Tropical Nights, Warmest 3-day Period and Climatological/Apparent Temperature Heatwave Days indices.
0.1 degree grid (~11km) - finer than most other indices in this source - via dedicated Fire Weather Index and High Fire Danger Days indices.
0.25 degree grid (~28km), via a dedicated Extreme Wind Speed Days index.
5km grid. Partial because only an indirect proxy (Aridity Actual index) exists - no dedicated water-stress index.
5km grid - finer than most other indices in this source - via dedicated Flood Recurrence and River Discharge indices.
0.25 degree grid (~28km), via dedicated Maximum Consecutive 5-Day Precipitation and Extreme Precipitation Total/Days indices.
0.25 degree grid (~28km) for the meteorological component (SPI-3); 5km grid for the soil-moisture component - resolution varies by sub-indicator.
NUTS 2/3 regional. Partial because only historical loss/damage event counts exist (Loss Data module, EM-DAT/media/Wikipedia-sourced); no modelled forward-looking hazard layer.
NUTS 2/3 regional, via the modelled Risk Analysis layer (EFFIS-derived Wildland-Urban Interface).
NUTS 2/3 regional. Partial because only historical loss/damage event counts exist (Loss Data module); no modelled forward-looking hazard layer.
NUTS 2/3 regional, via the modelled Risk Analysis layer.
NUTS 2/3 regional. Partial because only historical loss/damage event counts exist (Loss Data module, Flash Flood category); no modelled forward-looking hazard layer.
NUTS 2/3 regional. Partial because only historical loss/damage event counts exist (Loss Data module); no modelled forward-looking hazard layer.
200m/5km - finer than the source's overall NUTS 2/3 granularity - via the modelled Risk Analysis layer (ELSUS_v2 susceptibility layer plus GPCC precipitation).

Resolution varies by product: approximately 8-16km (fire danger forecast, ECMWF/MeteoFrance numerical weather models) versus 250m/20m (burnt-area perimeters, MODIS/Sentinel-2). The forecast grid is coarse relative to Austria's size - only a handful of cells cover the whole country.
0.25 degree grid (ERA5 soil-temperature-at-depth). Partial because no ready-made permafrost index exists - only raw variables usable as model input.

0.25 degree grid (~28km), via indices technically present in the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset. Partial because these are not a prominently findable feature of Copernicus CDS as a general-purpose entry point - practically accessed via Climate-ADAPT instead.

0.25 degree grid (~28km), via a derived index technically present in the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset, plus raw 10m wind-speed variables. Partial for the same not-prominently-findable reason as heat_wave.

0.25 degree grid (~28km), via derived indices technically present in the sis-ecde-climate-indicators dataset, plus raw precipitation variables. Partial for the same not-prominently-findable reason as heat_wave.

0.25 degree grid (~28km) for the meteorological component (SPI-3, derivable from raw precipitation); 5km grid via the standalone SMHI hydrology product for the soil-moisture component (see copernicus_climate_indicators) - resolution varies by sub-indicator and the meteorological part requires own processing.
0.25 degree grid (raw precipitation, soil-moisture and wind-speed variables). Partial because no ready-made erosion index exists - would require independent erosion modelling (e.g. RUSLE-type).
Institution/portfolio (bank-aggregate) level. Partial because this is EU supervisory reporting statistics, not spatially resolved to individual exposures.
Institution/portfolio (bank-aggregate) level. Partial because this is EU supervisory reporting statistics, not spatially resolved to individual exposures.
Parcel/cadastral level, via the official HQ30/HQ100/HQ300 flood hazard zone maps.
Grid. Partial because coverage and resolution vary by federal state - Starkregen-Gefahrenkarten (heavy-rain hazard maps) are not yet available everywhere.
Parcel/cadastral level where mapped. Partial because this covers torrent-related flood only, with incomplete national coverage.
Parcel/cadastral level, the core product of the official Gefahrenzonenplan (red/yellow zones).
Parcel/cadastral level, the core product of the official Gefahrenzonenplan (red/yellow zones).
Grid (~1km), daily wind-speed maps - coarser than the source's overall parcel-level granularity, and current-conditions rather than a long-term hazard zoning.
Parcel/cadastral level, based on the official flood risk zoning (Gefahrenzonenplan Fliessgewaesser).
Grid, derived from the same hydrological modelling as the flood layer - coarser than the source's overall parcel-level granularity, and less validated at parcel level.

Grid, indicative screening layer. Partial because this is newer and less mature than the flood layer, added via cooperation with GeoSphere Austria - coarser than the source's overall parcel-level granularity.
Sub-catchment (watershed) level, via dedicated baseline water stress, baseline water depletion, interannual variability, seasonal variability and groundwater table decline indicators.
Sub-catchment (watershed) level, via dedicated riverine flood risk and coastal flood risk indicators, not merely inferred from water-stress data.
Sub-catchment (watershed) level, via a dedicated drought risk indicator.
Facility/object level, proprietary modelled risk scores.
Facility/object level, proprietary modelled risk scores; wildfires is consistently named among Moody's six covered hazards.
Facility/object level, proprietary modelled risk scores.
Facility/object level, proprietary modelled risk scores.
Facility/object level. Partial because coverage is only advertised via the separate 'Climate Change Edition' ('13 climate hazards'), not individually named in the materials reviewed.
Facility/object level. Partial for the same unconfirmed-naming reason as heat_stress.
Facility/object level, explicitly named in the Natural Hazards Edition hazard list; a dedicated higher-resolution 'Wildfire HD Edition' is also available separately.
Facility/object level, explicitly named ('Extratropical Storm', the Europe-relevant category) in the Natural Hazards Edition hazard list.
Facility/object level. Partial for the same unconfirmed-naming reason as heat_stress.
Facility/object level, explicitly named (River Flood, Flash Flood, Storm Surge) in the Natural Hazards Edition hazard list.
Facility/object level. Partial because 'Flash Flood' is covered but classified and scored as a flood hazard, not a distinct heavy-precipitation indicator.
Facility/object level. Partial for the same unconfirmed-naming reason as heat_stress.
Facility/object level, explicitly named in the Natural Hazards Edition hazard list.
District (ADM2) level via ThinkHazard!'s public API, not merely country level - confirmed as one of the hazards with commonly-available probabilistic data.
District (ADM2) level via ThinkHazard!'s public API - confirmed as one of the hazards with commonly-available probabilistic data.

District (ADM2) level via ThinkHazard!'s 'cyclone' category. Partial because the terminology and hazard model are tropical-cyclone-oriented; applicability to European extratropical windstorms was not separately confirmed.
District (ADM2) level via ThinkHazard!'s public API, via a dedicated Water Stress Index (water availability per person per year).
District (ADM2) level via ThinkHazard!'s public API, covering river, urban and coastal flood.
District (ADM2) level. Partial because drought is not covered as a distinct event-based hazard - only indirectly inferable from the chronic Water Stress Index.
Continuous global grid - finer than the source's overall district-level granularity - via a dedicated Global Landslide Hazard Map (World Bank/GFDRR, commissioned from Arup).
1km grid, national, via daily precipitation (RR) fields since 1961, sufficient to derive a heavy-precipitation index directly.
1km grid, national, via daily min/max/mean temperature fields (TN, TX, TM, TM24) since 1961, sufficient to derive a heat-wave index directly.

1km grid, national. Partial because precipitation/temperature fields could support only a basic dryness proxy - the dedicated drought index (SPEI) is provided by the related WINFORE dataset, not SPARTACUS itself.
1km grid, national, via a dedicated SPEI (Standardized Precipitation Evapotranspiration Index) at 30/90/365-day aggregation - a purpose-built drought index.

1km grid, national. Partial because the climatic water balance (precipitation minus potential evapotranspiration) is drought/dryness-oriented, not a direct chronic water-stress (supply-vs-demand) indicator.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('coastal and riverine flooding') among modelled hazards.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('landslides') among modelled hazards.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('storms', 'tropical cyclones' and 'storm surge') among modelled hazards.
Asset/facility level. Partial because only the chronic 'heat stress' metric is confirmed by name; a distinct acute heat-wave product was not confirmed.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('heat stress') among modelled hazards.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('wildfires') among modelled hazards.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('flood') among the 9 modelled perils.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('tropical cyclones' and 'wind') among the 9 modelled perils; tropical-cyclone framing may limit direct Austria-relevance, as with Moody's.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('heat') among the 9 modelled perils.
Asset/facility level. Partial because only a general 'heat' peril is confirmed by name; whether this distinguishes acute (heat wave) from chronic (heat stress) was not confirmed.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('drought') among the 9 modelled perils.
Asset/facility level, explicitly confirmed ('wildfire') among the 9 modelled perils.
5km grid, via the standalone SMHI hydrology dataset (18 Climate Impact Indicators, including Flood Recurrence and River Discharge, directly selectable).
0.25 degree grid (~28km), via the standalone, peer-reviewed ERA5-HEAT dataset (hourly UTCI/mean radiant temperature, 1940-present).
5km grid, via the soil-moisture component (Mean Soil Moisture) of the standalone SMHI hydrology dataset. The meteorological/SPI-3 component remains raw-variable-only (see copernicus_cds).
5km grid, via the Aridity Actual indicator of the standalone SMHI hydrology dataset.
